newsitem.title: USA: USAir to buy up to 400 Airbus aircraft.
newsitem.headline: USAir to buy up to 400 Airbus aircraft.

text.p: USAir Group Inc said Wendesday it agreed to purchase 120 single-aisle Airbus Industrie aircraft, with options to buy up to 280 additional planes.
The deal, which will allow USAir to streamline its fleet and reduce costs, includes orders for Airbus A319, A320 and A321 models, the carrier said.
Because all three aircraft have the same cockpit, systems and common engine types, USAir said it will see operating cost reductions in crew training, scheduling and maintenance.

"USAir takes this important and significant step today in its effort to become the airline of choice and an airline with a competitive cost structure," said Stephen Wolf, USAir's chairman and chief executive officer said.
In addition to the firm orders, USAir has options for 120 additional aircraft with defined delivery dates and 160 other planes.

All three aircraft models feature fly-by-wire flight controls to reduce pilot workload, protect against windshear, stalling or overspeeding, reduce mechanical complexity and improve smoothness and stability, USAir said.
"Our production flexibility enables us to provide the aircraft on a schedule more suitable for the airline," Jean Pierson, managing director and chief executive officer of Airbus Industrie said.
